children: Private equity firm True North has acquired a minority stake worth around USD 50-60 million in adtech unicorn InMobi through secondary share purchases, as the SoftBank-backed company prepares for a proposed USD 1 billion initial public offering.

According to a media report, True North has acquired around 2-3 per cent of InMobi, with the bulk of the shares purchased from some of the company’s early investors seeking a partial exit. The transaction also included a small primary funding component.

Founded in 2007 by Naveen Tewari, Piyush Shah, Mohit Saxena and Abhay Singhal, InMobi provides marketing and monetisation solutions to brands, advertisers and publishers. The company also operates social commerce platform Roposo and Glance, its AI-powered Android lockscreen platform.

InMobi has raised more than USD 774 million to date from investors including SoftBank, Sherpalo Ventures and Kleiner Perkins. In June 2025, its co-founders invested around USD 3.7 million in the company. A few months later, the founders also repurchased a 25-30 per cent stake from SoftBank.

The company is currently redomiciling to India from Singapore as it prepares for a public listing. Earlier reports had indicated that InMobi had appointed JPMorgan Chase and Jefferies as advisors for its proposed IPO.
